correctness.rationale: Let P swap x and z and let F=P∘T be extended affinely from Q₄. The branch return is F², since the Q₂ branch is the swap-conjugate of the Q₄ branch. Direct determinant expansion gives the linear part K of F the polynomial r³+a²r−2ab; det(I−K²)=(1+a²−2ab)(1+a²+2ab)>0 for 0<b<1. The fixed point of F is therefore the only possible fixed point of the formal return, even if it falls outside the itinerary. Its sum and difference coordinates satisfy y=b(x+z), x−z=(2b−a)(x+z), x+z=a(x−z)+2, giving exactly the stated points and strict condition a<2b−1. For a≠0 the real root s has the sign of a and 0<|s|<1. Polynomial division gives the remaining roots −s/2±i sqrt(a²+3s²/4), whose squares are the nonreal return pair and have modulus a²+s². For a²<1 compare the increasing function t³+a²t at t=|s| and at t=sqrt(1−a²), where it equals t; this gives the claimed crossing at a²(1+4b²)=1. If a²≥1 the pair is expanding; at a=0 the return linear part is nilpotent and the existing cycle is a sink. At equality, s=2ab≠0 and K restricted to the center plane in basis (v,Kv) acts by (ξ,η)↦(−η,ξ−sη). Substitution preserves H=ξ²−sξη+η², which is positive definite since |s|<1. The invariant ellipses are exact for the affine return, not an approximation. The two strict quadrant visits hold on a neighborhood of U; small invariant neighborhoods for the return are obtained from sublevels of H plus a squared stable coordinate, which contracts by s². The first iterate stays near V on its affine branch and maps the center ellipses to nondegenerate companion ellipses because det K=2ab≠0 there. This gives Lyapunov stability and excludes attraction. Above the boundary the expanding real subspace is two-dimensional, with one transverse stable dimension.
